fuelEmissions.title: Fuel Emissions Calculator
fuelEmissions.intro: Avoided emissions of a candidate marine fuel against a fossil baseline, on the functional unit of energy delivered on board (MJ) - a tonne of green fuel does not replace a tonne of fossil fuel.
fuelEmissions.frameworkHelp: The same fuel has different official values under different frameworks - there is no 'the' emission factor, only a framework's. FuelEU Maritime: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 Annex II, GWP set AR4 (CH4 25, N2O 298). IMO Net-Zero: LCA Guidelines MEPC.391(81), AR5 (28/265), provisional. One framework selects every factor and the GWP set - values are never blended.
fuelEmissions.candidateWtwHelp: The candidate's certified WELL-TO-TANK intensity in gCO2e/MJ, from the Proof of Sustainability (the E-value documentation). Combustion N2O is added separately below - do not enter a well-to-wake figure here or the N2O slip double-counts (the RFNBO ceiling of 28.2 IS a well-to-wake number). There is no single default; certified renewable pathways typically land 5-15. Zero is not offered: a zero-emission pathway is an assumption, not a certifiable value.
fuelEmissions.baselineHelp: The 'avoided' number is only as honest as its baseline - it is user-selected, never silently assumed.
fuelEmissions.pilotShareHelp: Ammonia and methanol dual-fuel engines burn a fossil pilot for ignition - around 5% of energy, range 3-8% (MAN ES / WinGD full-engine testing). This puts a floor under the achievable reduction.
fuelEmissions.n2oScenarioHelp: THE dominant uncertainty: published values span a factor of 37, and neither FuelEU Annex II nor the IMO LCA Guidelines fixes an ammonia N2O default. The range is shown, never a bare point.
fuelEmissions.n2oRange: Published range: {low}-{high} g N2O per g NH3 (x37). Between best and worst, avoided emissions fall by ~48% and the fuel can stop qualifying as ZNZ.
fuelEmissions.efficiencyRatioHelp: Alternative-fuel engine efficiency vs the baseline engine's. MAN full-engine testing indicates similar thermal efficiency in diesel and ammonia mode for two-stroke dual-fuel engines, so 1.0 is the evidenced default rather than an omission.
fuelEmissions.notParameterised: Not parameterised: {fuel} cannot be evaluated under this framework.
fuelEmissions.directionReverse: From fossil to zero / near-zero (ZNZ) fuel
fuelEmissions.certifiedRange: Certified pathway values for {fuel} span {low}-{high} gCO2e/MJ.
fuelEmissions.blendHelp: The candidate side's emissions over TOTAL delivered energy — fuel plus its fossil pilot — in gCO2e/MJ. Under the IMO framework this is the ship-side attained-GFI analogue, tested against the reduction ladder (not modelled here) — NOT the ZNZ threshold: a fuel can be ZNZ while its blend sits above the line.
fuelEmissions.znzTo2034: The fuel counts as zero / near-zero until 2034 (needs ≤ {threshold})
fuelEmissions.znzFrom2035: The fuel counts as zero / near-zero from 2035 (needs ≤ {threshold})
fuelEmissions.znzHelp: Zero / near-zero eligibility under the IMO Net-Zero Framework applies to the well-to-wake GHG intensity of the FUEL or energy source itself — including its own combustion terms and the ammonia N2O slip, excluding pilot fuel: at most 19.0 gCO2e/MJ until end-2034, 14.0 from 2035 (MEPC 83 approved text; IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQ, verified 2026-08-14). The ship's attained GFI (the blend above) is a different test.
fuelEmissions.citation: Method: energy-delivered comparison (MJ), never tonne-for-tonne; emission factors and GWP set {gwp} per {framework}; dataset {version}.
fuelEmissions.citationSubstituted: Substituted from FuelEU Annex II, no confirmed IMO value (marked unverified above): {factors}.
fuelEmissions.imoSubstitution: No confirmed IMO value - substituted from FuelEU Annex II and disclosed in the method line.
fuelEmissions.wttInversion: The candidate's upstream (well-to-tank) emissions exceed the fossil baseline's - {cand} vs {base} tCO2e. Every tonne of the saving is combustion-side; this is why the comparison is well-to-wake.
fuelEmissions.intensityHelp: Candidate vs baseline GHG intensity in gCO2e/MJ, on the selected basis. References: IMO 2008 fleet average {gfi}; FuelEU 2020 baseline {feu}.
fuelEmissions.footer: Dataset {version} - every factor carries its citation (tooltips); estimates from framework defaults and your inputs, not compliance advice.
fuelEmissions.equivalentHelp: The energy-equivalence line: masses are converted through each fuel's energy density (MJ/t). Tonne-for-tonne comparison overstates avoided emissions by more than 2x for ammonia.
